parents.name: Perry's economic returns are sufficient grounds to expand publicly funded preschool for disadvantaged children.
parents.description: This policy judgment favors expansion based on Perry's modeled long-term benefits. Whether those benefits would transfer to new programs remains a separate evidentiary question.

parents.name: Expanding publicly funded preschool for disadvantaged children requires evidence beyond Perry's economic returns.
parents.description: This policy judgment calls for evidence about the programs and populations proposed for expansion. It does not deny the positive returns estimated for Perry itself.

evidence.interpretation: Alternative murder valuation of the same study/model; not independent support or replication.

evidence.name: Perry's modeled lifetime returns include projected earnings beyond the study's age-40 follow-up.
evidence.description: Heckman and colleagues (2010) extend earnings profiles through age 65 using outside data. They also estimate returns with benefits ending at age 40 to examine sensitivity to extrapolation.
evidence.sourceLocator: Introduction p.115; Section 3 p.117; Section 3.2.2 p.119; Section 4.3 pp.125-126

evidence.name: Perry's modeled societal benefit/cost ratio remains 5.4 when benefits end at age 40, at a 3% discount rate.
evidence.description: Heckman and colleagues (2010), Table 7, report SE 2.2 for the pooled sample, using the $13,000 murder valuation and $0.50 tax-financing welfare loss per tax dollar. This scenario omits benefits after age 40 but still uses imputation and economic valuation.
evidence.sourceLocator: Table 7, printed p.126 / PDF page 13; Separate arrest ratios, low murder cost, pooled sample
evidence.mappingRequirement: Use typed existing ratio, SE, discount, welfare-loss, valuation, perspective and population properties; verify an age-endpoint field distinct from elapsed follow-up. Do not silently label this a 40-year follow-up or a directly observed causal ratio. Reuse the Table 1 age-65 comparator instead of creating a duplicate Table 7 cell.

pairReview.reason: Opposite judgments about whether Perry's economic returns are sufficient grounds for expansion; neither is a paper conclusion.
Positive modeled net social benefits supply an economic argument for expansion without proving transportability.
This parent explicitly accepts Perry's positive model results; those results alone do not contradict its demand for additional evidence.
A modeling assumption qualifies the inference but does not itself refute a policy judgment.
Extrapolation within Perry is distinct from evidence of generalization to new programs; do not force support for the transportability claim.
Different valuation assumptions materially change the assertion; neither duplicate nor independent replication.
Same study sensitivity case qualifies the lifetime supporter; avoid presenting two horizons as independent evidence.
Positive within-follow-up modeled benefits do not resolve transferability; they prevent an exaggerated claim that all benefits require later extrapolation.
The age-40 result is a complementary sensitivity finding, not a contradiction of the lifetime model's use of projections.
Same population and assumptions with distinct benefit horizons; expose paired comparison rather than duplicate evidence counts.
